questions.question: A friend says to you, *'I’ve been meaning to ask you—could you help me move these boxes tomorrow afternoon?'* What would be the most appropriate response if you are busy but want to politely decline?
options: Of course, I’d love to help! What time would suit you?
I’m sorry, I’m afraid I can’t this time—I’ve already got plans for the afternoon.
You’re welcome! Just let me know when you need me.
Moving boxes? That sounds fun! Maybe next week then?
questions.answer: I’m sorry, I’m afraid I can’t this time—I’ve already got plans for the afternoon.

questions.question: Your colleague mentions their new hobby: *'I’ve started knitting scarves for charity—it’s really relaxing!'*. How would you respond if you agree but want to add a critical opinion about their choice?
options: That sounds lovely! I wish I had time to try it too.
I’m glad you find it relaxing—it’s a bit unusual for me, but I admire your commitment!
Knitting sounds fun, but I think it’s a waste of time compared to reading.
I’m sure your scarves will be perfect for charity—keep up the good work!
questions.answer: I’m glad you find it relaxing—it’s a bit unusual for me, but I admire your commitment!

questions.question: At a social gathering, someone asks: *'Do you think we should move the meeting to the afternoon?'* What would be the most polite way to suggest an alternative time if you’re busy?
options: Yes, definitely—afternoon is better for everyone.
I’m afraid I’m not available then, but maybe tomorrow morning would work?
That’s a great idea! Let’s do it tomorrow instead.
I’ll check my schedule and get back to you on that.
questions.answer: I’m afraid I’m not available then, but maybe tomorrow morning would work?

questions.question: Your boss asks you: *'Can you explain the project’s timeline to the team?'* What would be the most appropriate response if you want to offer to help but also ask for clarification first?
options: Of course, I’ll prepare a detailed report and send it to you tomorrow.
I’m happy to help, but could you clarify which part of the timeline you’re referring to?
That sounds like a lot of work—I’ll see what I can do.
The timeline is already clear in the meeting notes—let’s discuss it then.
questions.answer: I’m happy to help, but could you clarify which part of the timeline you’re referring to?

questions.question: A stranger on the street asks: *'Excuse me, could you tell me where the nearest library is?'* How would you respond if you want to be polite but also ask them to confirm their location first?
options: The nearest library is two blocks that way—thanks for asking!
I’m sorry, I don’t know the area well—I’ll ask someone else.
You’re welcome! It’s on High Street, but let me check my map.
Could you tell me where you’re standing so I can point it out to you?
questions.answer: Could you tell me where you’re standing so I can point it out to you?
